notes: MST baseline. Unweighted (BFS spanning forest) is the fastest path; Kruskal beats Prim on every input shape (10-25x), which is the expected pattern for our `std::cmp::Reverse<BinaryHeap>` Prim against a sort-once Kruskal — `slice::sort_unstable_by` is cache-friendly and amortizes one O(m log m) pass, while Prim pays log-m per push and a heap-stale-skip per pop. Automatic dispatch on weighted input matches Kruskal up to a constant. Sparse n=10000 surfaces the m log m vs m * log m crossover (BFS still dominates when weights are absent). A future perf pass could swap Prim's heap for a d-ary or indexed heap (mirrors upstream `igraph_d_indheap` in spanning_trees.c:176) to close the Prim gap; not on the critical path for v0.0.1.
